en.name: Dwaeji-gukbap
en.summary: Busan's soul food: rice in a milky pork-bone broth
en.ingredients: Pork-bone broth, boiled pork suyuk (shoulder, belly, jowl, etc.), rice, seasoned chives, saeujeot (salted shrimp), dadaegi (chili paste)
en.taste: A rich, savory meat broth with tender sliced pork, finished salty and clean with salted shrimp and chives
en.origin: The most widely held story is that it caught on during the Korean War, when refugees crowding into Busan simmered cheap pork bones and offal for a long time. Another theory traces it to the market-day gukbap of Miryang, Hapcheon and other parts of South Gyeongsang.
steps: First taste a spoonful of the plain broth to get its natural flavor.
Add plenty of seasoned chives (jeongguji) and season with saeujeot (salted shrimp).
For a spicier kick, stir in dadaegi (chili paste) a little at a time.
Either stir the rice into the soup or eat them separately, ttaro-gukbap style, and dip the pork in salted shrimp.
en.tip: Season with salted shrimp rather than salt to add depth of umami to the broth.
en.allergenNote: Whether wheat noodles (somyeon) are served, what goes into the dadaegi, and whether beef-bone broth (sagol) is blended in vary by restaurant.

zh.name: 猪肉汤饭
zh.summary: 把米饭泡进奶白猪骨汤里吃的釜山灵魂美食
zh.ingredients: 猪骨高汤、白切猪肉（前腿肉、五花肉、猪颈肉等）、米饭、凉拌韭菜、虾酱、辣酱（dadaegi）
zh.taste: 香浓醇厚的肉汤配软嫩白切肉，用虾酱和韭菜调出咸香清爽的收尾
zh.origin: 较有力的说法是：朝鲜战争时期涌入釜山的难民用便宜的猪骨和下水长时间熬汤，这道菜由此普及。也有说法认为它源自密阳、陕川等庆尚南道地区的集市汤饭。
steps: 先不加任何东西，舀一勺汤品尝原味。
放入大量凉拌韭菜（当地叫 jeongguji），再用虾酱调咸淡。
想吃辣可以一点点拌入辣酱（dadaegi）。
把米饭泡进汤里吃，或像 ttaro-gukbap 那样汤饭分开吃；肉可以蘸虾酱吃。
zh.tip: 用虾酱而不是盐来调味，汤会更加鲜美。
zh.allergenNote: 是否提供素面、辣酱的原料、是否混入牛骨高汤，各店不同。

ja.summary: 白濁した豚骨スープにご飯を入れて食べる釜山のソウルフード
ja.ingredients: 豚骨スープ、ゆで豚スユク（肩肉・バラ肉・豚トロなど）、ご飯、ニラの和え物、セウジョッ（アミの塩辛）、タデギ（薬味ダレ）
ja.taste: 香ばしく濃厚な肉スープに柔らかいゆで豚、アミの塩辛とニラで塩気とすっきり感を添えた味
ja.origin: 朝鮮戦争の際に釜山へ押し寄せた避難民が、安い豚骨や副産物をじっくり煮込んで食べたことで広まったという説が有力です。密陽・陜川など慶尚南道の市場クッパがルーツだという説もあります。
steps: まず何も入れずにスープをひと口すくい、素の味を確かめます。
ニラの和え物（チョングジ）をたっぷり入れ、アミの塩辛で塩加減を整えます。
辛みが欲しければタデギ（薬味ダレ）を少しずつ溶かします。
ご飯をスープに入れるか、タロクッパのように別々に食べ、肉はアミの塩辛につけて食べます。
ja.tip: 塩ではなくアミの塩辛で味付けすると、スープにうま味が加わります。
ja.allergenNote: 素麺の有無、タデギの材料、牛骨スープを混ぜるかどうかは店によって異なります。

en.name: Milmyeon
en.summary: Busan's refreshing take on naengmyeon, made with wheat flour by war refugees
en.ingredients: Wheat flour and starch noodles, beef-bone or medicinal-herb broth, yangnyeom-jang (spicy sauce), sliced boiled meat (pyeonyuk), cucumber, boiled egg (or egg ribbons)
en.taste: Chewy wheat noodles in a sweet-tangy, slushy iced broth with a spicy sauce, cool and refreshing
en.origin: It began after the Korean War, when refugees from the North who settled in Busan made noodles from wheat flour, plentiful as aid supplies, instead of the usual naengmyeon ingredients. Naeho Naengmyeon, opened in Uam-dong, Nam-gu in 1953, is regarded as the birthplace of milmyeon.
steps: Before eating, add vinegar and mustard to taste.
If the noodles are long, cut them once or twice with scissors.
Stir the spicy sauce evenly into the broth, then eat it with the noodles.
Sip the warm broth (on-yuksu) served alongside now and then to settle your stomach.
en.tip: Broths differ a lot from shop to shop, so first-timers can start with mul-milmyeon (in broth) and have fun comparing several places.
en.allergenNote: Broth ingredients (beef bone, chicken, medicinal herbs) and the type of meat garnish vary by shop; some use chicken broth.

zh.name: 小麦冷面
zh.summary: 难民用面粉做出的釜山式清凉冷面
zh.ingredients: 面粉和淀粉制的面条、牛骨或中药材高汤、辣酱、白切肉片、黄瓜、煮鸡蛋（或蛋皮丝）
zh.taste: 酸甜带冰碴的汤底，配上筋道的小麦面和香辣酱汁，清凉爽口
zh.origin: 朝鲜战争后，从北方南下定居釜山的失乡民用作为援助物资而随处可得的面粉代替冷面原料制作面条，由此诞生。1953年在南区牛岩洞开业的“内湖冷面”被视为小麦冷面的发源地。
steps: 吃之前依个人口味加醋和芥末。
面条太长的话，用剪刀剪一两下。
把辣酱均匀化开在汤里，再和面条一起吃。
边吃边喝一口随餐附上的热肉汤，暖暖胃。
zh.tip: 各家汤底风味差异很大，第一次吃可以从汤面（mul-milmyeon）开始，多比较几家也很有乐趣。
zh.allergenNote: 汤底原料（牛骨、鸡、中药材）和配料肉的种类各店不同，也有店家使用鸡汤。

ja.name: ミルミョン
ja.summary: 避難民が小麦粉で作った釜山式のさっぱり冷麺
ja.ingredients: 小麦粉・でんぷんの麺、牛骨または漢方スープ、ヤンニョムジャン（辛味ダレ）、ゆで肉の薄切り、きゅうり、ゆで卵（または錦糸卵）
ja.taste: 甘酸っぱいシャーベット状のスープにもちもちの小麦麺、ピリ辛のヤンニョムジャンが調和した爽やかな味
ja.origin: 朝鮮戦争後に北から逃れて釜山に定着した失郷民が、冷麺の材料の代わりに援助物資で手に入りやすくなった小麦粉で麺を作ったのが始まりです。1953年に南区牛岩洞で開業した内湖冷麺がミルミョン発祥の店とされています。
steps: 食べる前に酢とからしを好みで加えます。
麺が長ければハサミで1〜2回切ります。
ヤンニョムジャンをスープによく溶かし混ぜてから、麺と一緒に食べます。
一緒に出る温かいスープを合間に飲んで、お腹を落ち着かせます。
ja.tip: 店ごとにスープの味がかなり違うので、初めてならムルミルミョン（汁あり）から始めて何軒か食べ比べるのも楽しみです。
ja.allergenNote: スープの材料（牛骨・鶏・漢方）やトッピングの肉の種類は店によって異なり、鶏スープを使う店もあります。

en.name: Ssiat-hotteok
en.summary: Nampo-dong's famous fried hotteok packed with nutty seeds
en.ingredients: Glutinous rice and wheat dough, brown-sugar syrup, nuts and seeds such as sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, peanuts and pine nuts, margarine
en.taste: Crisp outside and chewy inside, with sweet brown-sugar syrup and crunchy, nutty seeds
en.origin: Hotteok came to Korea in the modern era through ethnic Chinese immigrants, and the style of splitting a fried hotteok and stuffing it with seeds is said to have started at street stalls on BIFF Square in Nampo-dong. It became famous nationwide after appearing on the TV variety show '2 Days & 1 Night' and is now Busan's signature snack.
steps: Line up at a stall and order a hotteok fresh out of the fryer.
The hotteok is split in half, stuffed with plenty of seeds, and handed to you in a paper cup or on a sheet of paper.
The melted sugar syrup is very hot, so let it cool a little and bite from the top.
Finish it while it's warm as you stroll BIFF Square and the alleys of Gukje Market.
en.tip: Takeaway cools down and loses its crispness, so it tastes best eaten on the spot.
en.allergenNote: The mix of seeds and nuts and the frying margarine (may contain milk and soy) vary by stall.

zh.summary: 油炸糖饼里塞满香脆坚果种子的南浦洞名小吃

zh.origin: 糖饼在近代经由华侨传入韩国，而把油炸糖饼切开、塞入坚果种子的吃法，据说起源于南浦洞BIFF广场的路边摊。在综艺节目《两天一夜》中出现后闻名全国，成为釜山代表小吃。
steps: 在摊位前排队，点一个刚炸好的糖饼。
糖饼对半切开、塞满坚果种子后，用纸杯或纸包着递给你。
融化的糖浆非常烫，稍微放凉后从上面开始咬。
边逛BIFF广场和国际市场的小巷，边趁热吃完。
zh.tip: 打包带走会变凉、失去酥脆口感，现场马上吃最好吃。
zh.allergenNote: 种子与坚果的搭配，以及油炸用的人造黄油（可能含乳制品、大豆成分），各摊位不同。

BIFF広場や国際市場の路地を歩きながら、温かいうちに食べきります。
ja.tip: 持ち帰ると冷めてサクサク感がなくなるので、その場ですぐ食べるのがいちばんおいしいです。

en.name: Nakgopsae
en.summary: A spicy hot pot of small octopus, beef tripe and shrimp from the Jobang alleys
en.ingredients: Small octopus (nakji), beef small intestine (gopchang), shrimp, onion, green onion, glass noodles, chili-flake and gochujang sauce
en.taste: A rich, hot-and-sweet sauce with chewy octopus, savory tripe fat and springy shrimp
en.origin: It is said to have started in the octopus stir-fry restaurants around 'Jobang' in Beomil-dong, Dong-gu, once home to the Joseon Spinning mill, where gopchang and shrimp were added to the nakji bokkeum loved by workers. As places like Jobang Nakji and Gaemijip became famous, it grew into a signature Busan dish.
steps: When the ingredients arrive in the hot-pot pan, turn on the heat and stir as it simmers so the sauce coats everything.
Once the tripe and shrimp are cooked, put rice in a large bowl and spoon the nakgopsae over it with the sauce.
Top with the bean sprouts, chives and seaweed flakes served alongside, and mix it all together.
Finish by stir-frying rice in the leftover sauce (bokkeumbap).
en.tip: Order it mild at first; it gets spicier as the sauce reduces, so mix it with your rice while there is still broth.
en.allergenNote: Octopus is not a mandatory labeled allergen, but take care if you are allergic to mollusks; add-on noodles (sari) and sauce ingredients vary by restaurant.

zh.name: 章鱼肥肠虾火锅
zh.summary: 将小章鱼、牛肥肠和虾一起辣煮的朝纺巷火锅
zh.ingredients: 小章鱼、牛小肠（肥肠）、虾、洋葱、大葱、粉条、辣椒粉和辣椒酱调料
zh.taste: 香辣微甜的酱汁里，有筋道的章鱼、油香的肥肠和弹牙的虾，味道浓郁
zh.origin: 据说起源于东区凡一洞昔日“朝鲜纺织”所在的“朝纺”一带的炒章鱼店——在工人们爱吃的炒章鱼里加入肥肠和虾。随着“朝纺章鱼（조방낙지）”“蚂蚁之家（개미집）”等店走红，成为釜山代表美食。
steps: 食材装在火锅盘中上桌后，开火边搅拌边煮，让酱汁均匀入味。
肥肠和虾熟了以后，在大碗里盛饭，连汤带料舀到饭上。
放上随餐的豆芽、韭菜和海苔碎，拌匀后吃。
最后用剩下的酱汁炒饭收尾。
zh.tip: 一开始先点微辣，酱汁收干后会越来越辣，趁还有汤汁时拌饭吃。
zh.allergenNote: 章鱼虽不属于强制标示的过敏原，但对软体动物过敏者请注意；加点的面类和酱料原料各店不同。

en.name: Eomuk
en.summary: Busan's signature chewy fish cake made from fish paste

en.price: ₩1,000–1,500 per skewer; ₩2,500–4,500 for fish-cake croquettes and hot bars
en.origin: Fish cake came to Korea as Japanese kamaboko during the Japanese colonial period. After Korea's liberation and the Korean War, fish-cake factories around Bupyeong Market (today's Kkangtong Market) and Yeongdo made it in large quantities, and the name 'Busan eomuk' took hold. Many shops are now run by the third generation, such as Samjin Eomuk, which opened in Yeongdo in 1953.
steps: Pick a fish-cake skewer warming in the street stall's broth pot.

When you finish, pay by counting your skewers. At fish-cake shops, also try eomuk croquettes or hot bars.
en.tip: On cold days you can refill your broth as often as you like, so warm up with a few skewers.
en.allergenNote: Some fish cakes contain shrimp, squid, crab meat, cheese or egg white, so check the label for each kind.

en.name: Haeundae Amso-galbi
en.summary: Haeundae's famous Hanwoo cow short ribs, grilled over charcoal

en.name: Naengchae-jokbal
en.gloss: Cold pig's trotters with jellyfish & mustard
en.summary: Busan-style jokbal (pig's trotters) tossed with jellyfish, vegetables and a sharp mustard sauce
en.ingredients: Thinly sliced jokbal (pig's trotters), jellyfish, cucumber, onion, carrot and other vegetables, mustard sauce (mustard, vinegar, sugar; some places add oyster sauce or soy sauce)
en.taste: Chewy trotters and crunchy jellyfish meet a sweet-and-sour mustard sauce with a sinus-tingling kick, cool and refreshing.
en.origin: The dish was born in the early 1980s in the jokbal alley of Bupyeong-dong, Jung-gu. It is said to combine naengchae (cold salad) with the jokbal culture of people displaced from the North who settled in Busan after the Korean War. Busan Jokbal in Nampo-dong is known as the place that first created it.
steps: When the platter arrives, toss the trotters, jellyfish and vegetables evenly with the mustard sauce.
Pick up a slice of trotter together with jellyfish and cucumber and eat it in one bite.
If the sauce runs short, ask for more and coat the meat generously.
Enjoy it as anju (drinking food) with ice-cold soju or beer.
en.tip: Waits in Bupyeong-dong's jokbal alley get long in the evening, so go for an early dinner, or get takeout and enjoy it at your accommodation.
en.allergenNote: Whether the sauce contains oyster sauce or soy sauce, whether egg garnish (jidan) is added, and whether salted shrimp (saeujeot) is served on the side varies by restaurant.

en.name: Gijang Daege
en.summary: Snow crab picked from the tanks at Gijang Market and steamed on the spot
en.ingredients: Snow crab (mostly imported Russian crab; domestic crab only in season), rice, gim (laver) and sesame oil for crab-shell fried rice
en.taste: A briny sea aroma, sweet and juicy leg meat, and the rich, nutty flavor of the crab innards.
en.price: Market price (approx. ₩60,000–100,000 per kg; table-setting charge extra)
en.origin: Gijang Market in Gijang-eup, Gijang-gun, is lined with crab restaurants that steam whichever crab you pick from the tanks, and it has become known as the place in Busan to go for snow crab. Russian snow crab, which makes up most of the snow crab sold in Korea, is relatively affordable here, so locals and travelers come in large numbers.
steps: Choose a crab from the market tank, have it weighed, check the price, then leave it to be steamed.
Bend each leg joint backward and pull; the meat slides out in one piece, ready to eat.
Pick out the body meat and dip it in the innards inside the shell.
Finish by adding rice to the empty shell for crab-shell fried rice.
en.tip: Parking around the market is tough on weekends, so walking from Gijang Station on the Donghae Line is easier. Always confirm the weight and price before it is steamed.
en.allergenNote: Whether egg or soy sauce goes into the crab-shell fried rice, and which side dishes are served (steamed egg, fried shrimp, etc.), varies by restaurant.

en.name: Kkomjangeo-gui
en.summary: Busan's classic drinking dish: hagfish grilled over briquettes or a straw fire until pleasantly chewy
en.ingredients: Hagfish (meokjangeo, also called gomjangeo), onion, green onion, salt or gochujang seasoning
en.taste: Chewy with a crunchy bite and rich, savory fat; the spicy version is sweet and hot, while straw-fire grilling gives a deep smoky aroma.
en.origin: It is said to have started near Jagalchi during the Japanese colonial era, when people grilled the hagfish meat left over after the skins were stripped for leather goods. Refugees ate it widely during the Korean War, giving rise to Jagalchi's hagfish alley. In Gijang, jjippul gomjangeo, whole hagfish grilled over a rice-straw fire, is famous.
steps: Choose salt-grilled (sogeum-gui) or spicy (yangnyeom-gui); straw-fire grilled (jjippul-gui) is served at Gijang specialty restaurants.
Cook on the grill or foil until golden outside and firm and chewy.
Dip salt-grilled hagfish in sesame-oil salt (gireumjang) or plain salt; for straw-fire grilled, peel off the charred skin first, then dip in salt sauce.
For the spicy version, finish by stir-frying rice in the leftover sauce.
en.tip: If it's your first time, start with salt-grilled to taste the hagfish itself, then order the spicy version next time.
en.allergenNote: Salt-grilled hagfish contains almost none of the allergens that must be labeled, but the gochujang and soy sauce seasoning of the spicy version contains soybean and wheat, and sauce ingredients vary by restaurant.

en.name: Dongnae Pajeon
en.summary: Dongnae's local pancake of whole green onions and seafood cooked in a rice-flour batter
en.ingredients: Whole jjokpa (slender green onions), seafood such as oyster, mussel, clam meat and shrimp, beef (at some places), glutinous and non-glutinous rice-flour batter (sometimes mixed with wheat flour), anchovy broth, egg
en.taste: Moist and chewy rather than crispy, with sweet green onion and rich seafood flavor; it pairs well with chogochujang (vinegared chili paste).
en.calories: About 500 kcal (per person, about half a pancake)
en.origin: A local dish once sold at the Dongnae market. Residents' oral accounts say it was offered to the king around Samjinnal (the 3rd day of the 3rd lunar month), but this is not confirmed in records. Dongnae Halmae Pajeon, said to have started at the Dongnae market around 1940 and now in its fourth generation, made it widely known.
steps: The pancake arrives with green onions laid side by side, rice-flour batter poured over and cooked, then topped with seafood and egg; dig in while it's hot.
Divide it into bite-size pieces with chopsticks or scissors and pick up green onion and seafood together.
Dipping in chogochujang instead of soy sauce is the Dongnae way.
Enjoy with makgeolli or dongdongju (rice wine).
en.tip: Parking around Dongnae Halmae Pajeon is difficult, so walk from Suan Station (Line 4) or Dongnae Station (Line 1).
en.allergenNote: The ratio of wheat to rice flour in the batter and the kinds of seafood and beef on top vary by restaurant; chogochujang contains wheat and soybean from the gochujang.

zh.name: 东莱葱饼
zh.summary: 整根细香葱和海鲜用米粉面糊煎成的东莱乡土葱饼
zh.ingredients: 整根细香葱（jjokpa）、牡蛎·贻贝·蛤蜊肉·虾等海鲜、牛肉（视店家而定）、糯米·粳米粉面糊（有时掺面粉）、鳀鱼高汤、鸡蛋
zh.taste: 不追求酥脆，而是湿润软糯；香葱的甜味和海鲜的鲜味浓郁，配醋辣椒酱（chogochujang）格外搭。
zh.origin: 原是东莱集市上售卖的乡土食物。据居民口述，三月三（上巳节）前后曾进贡给国王，但并无文献记载可证。据说约1940年在东莱集市开始营业的「东莱奶奶葱饼（동래할매파전）」传承四代，让这道菜广为人知。
steps: 葱饼是整齐铺好细香葱、浇上米粉面糊煎熟，再放上海鲜和鸡蛋端上桌的，请趁热享用。
用筷子或剪刀分成一口大小，把葱和海鲜一起夹起。
不蘸酱油而蘸醋辣椒酱，才是东莱吃法。
配上马格利或东东酒一起享用。
zh.tip: 东莱奶奶葱饼周边不好停车，建议从地铁4号线寿安站或1号线东莱站步行前往。
zh.allergenNote: 面糊中面粉与米粉的比例，以及所放海鲜和牛肉的种类，各店不同；醋辣椒酱中含有来自辣椒酱的小麦和大豆。

ja.name: 東莱パジョン
ja.summary: 丸ごとのワケギと海鮮を米粉の生地で焼いた、東莱の郷土チヂミ
ja.ingredients: 丸ごとのワケギ（チョッパ）、カキ・ムール貝・アサリのむき身・エビなどの海鮮、牛肉（店による）、もち米粉・うるち米粉の生地（小麦粉を混ぜることも）、煮干しだし、卵
ja.taste: カリッというよりしっとりもちもち。ワケギの甘みと海鮮のうまみが濃く、酢コチュジャン（チョコチュジャン）とよく合います。
ja.origin: 東莱の市場で売られていた郷土料理で、サムジンナル（旧暦3月3日）の頃に王様に献上したという話が住民の口伝で伝わっていますが、記録では確認されていません。1940年頃に東莱の市場で商売を始めたとされる「東莱ハルメパジョン（동래할매파전）」が4代にわたって受け継ぎ、広く知られるようになりました。
steps: ワケギを並べて米粉の生地を流して焼き、海鮮と卵をのせて出てくるパジョンを熱いうちにいただきます。
箸やはさみでひと口大に分け、ワケギと海鮮を一緒につまみます。
しょうゆではなく酢コチュジャンにつけるのが東莱流です。
マッコリやトンドンジュと一緒に楽しみます。
ja.tip: 東莱ハルメパジョン周辺は駐車が難しいので、地下鉄4号線・寿安（スアン）駅か1号線・東莱駅から歩くのが便利です。
allergens: 貝類（カキ・アワビ・ムール貝を含む）
ja.allergenNote: 生地の小麦粉と米粉の割合、のせる海鮮や牛肉の種類は店によって異なり、酢コチュジャンにはコチュジャン由来の小麦と大豆が含まれます。

en.name: Bokguk
en.summary: Busan's clear pufferfish hangover soup with bean sprouts and minari
en.ingredients: Pufferfish (eunbok, kkachibok, milbok, chambok), bean sprouts, minari (water dropwort), radish, garlic, kelp broth
en.taste: A clear, refreshing broth lifted by the fresh scent of minari, with mild, chewy pufferfish. A few drops of vinegar make the broth taste even cleaner.
en.origin: In Busan, where pufferfish is caught and traded in large amounts, clear pufferfish soup became a staple hangover soup. Kumsu Bokguk, which opened in Haeundae in 1970 as 'Kumsu Sikjang', is known as the first place to serve bokguk cooked one portion at a time in an earthenware ttukbaegi, and the dish went on to become a popular Busan food.
steps: When the soup arrives, taste the broth first, then add two or three drops of vinegar for a cleaner flavor.
Lift the bean sprouts and minari out onto your rice, add the seasoning sauce and mix.
Pick the pufferfish meat off the bone and dip it lightly in wasabi soy sauce (or vinegar soy sauce).
Finish by putting your rice into the remaining hot broth.
en.tip: It's an ideal hangover breakfast the morning after drinking. First-timers can start with eunbok jiri (clear silver pufferfish soup), the most affordable option.
en.allergenNote: Bean sprouts and the soy-sauce seasoning bring in soy and wheat. Some places make a spicy maeuntang version with chili flakes or use a seafood broth.

zh.name: 河豚汤
zh.summary: 加黄豆芽和水芹清炖的釜山解酒河豚汤
zh.ingredients: 河豚(银河豚 eunbok、条纹河豚 kkachibok、milbok、虎河豚 chambok)、黄豆芽、水芹(minari)、萝卜、大蒜、海带高汤
zh.taste: 汤底清澈爽口,水芹香气清新,河豚肉清淡有嚼劲。加一点醋,汤味会更清爽。
zh.origin: 釜山河豚捕捞量和流通量大,清炖河豚汤因此成为当地常见的解酒汤。1970年以"Kumsu Sikjang"之名在海云台开业的Kumsu Bokguk(금수복국),据说是最早用砂锅(ttukbaegi)一人一份煮河豚汤的店,河豚汤由此成为大众化的釜山美食。
steps: 上桌后先尝一口汤,再滴两三滴醋,让汤味更清爽。
把汤里的黄豆芽和水芹捞到米饭上,加酱料拌着吃。
把河豚肉剔下来,轻蘸芥末酱油(或醋酱油)食用。
最后把米饭泡进剩下的热汤里收尾。
zh.tip: 非常适合喝酒后第二天早上解酒。第一次吃的话,可以先从价格实惠的银河豚清汤(eunbok jiri)开始。
zh.allergenNote: 黄豆芽和酱油调味料含大豆、小麦;部分店家会做成加辣椒粉的辣汤(maeuntang),或使用海鲜高汤。

ja.name: ポックク(フグ汁)
ja.summary: 豆もやしとセリを入れて澄んだスープに仕上げる釜山の二日酔い向けフグ汁
ja.category: 汁物・鍋(ヘジャンクク/酔い覚ましスープ)

ja.taste: 澄んだすっきりスープにセリの香りが爽やかで、フグの身は淡白で歯ごたえがある。酢を少し加えるとスープがさらにさっぱりする。
ja.origin: フグの水揚げと流通が多い釜山では、フグを澄んだスープに仕立てたポッククが酔い覚ましの定番になりました。1970年に海雲台で「クムス食場」として開業したクムスポッククが、トゥッペギ(土鍋)で1人前ずつ煮て出すポッククを初めて提供した店として知られ、釜山の大衆的な料理になりました。

スープの豆もやしとセリをご飯にのせ、ヤンニョムジャン(たれ)を加えて混ぜて食べる。
フグの身をほぐし、わさび醤油(または酢醤油)に軽くつけて食べる。
残ったスープにご飯を入れて、熱々で締める。

en.name: Bibim-dangmyeon
en.summary: A market favorite: glass noodles topped with fish cake, pickled radish and chives, mixed together
en.ingredients: Dangmyeon (sweet-potato starch noodles), fish cake (eomuk), danmuji (yellow pickled radish), garlic chives and spinach, soy-sauce seasoning, chili flakes, sesame seeds
en.taste: Chewy, slippery glass noodles soak up a sweet-salty sauce, nutty like japchae with a gentle spicy kick.
en.origin: It is said to have been a hunger-filling dish sold at stalls in Gukje Market and Bupyeong Kkangtong Market during the Korean War refugee years. Instead of full japchae, vendors cheaply served boiled glass noodles with just toppings and seasoning sauce, and this Busan market food has carried on to this day.
steps: Mix the noodles and sauce thoroughly with chopsticks, just as served, until the color is even.
Pick up the shredded fish cake, pickled radish and chives together with the noodles in one bite.
Sip the fish-cake broth served on the side now and then to refresh your palate.
Order Chungmu gimbap or multteok (rice cake skewers in broth) alongside, market-style.
en.tip: Go in the evening when the Kkangtong Market night market is open to try bibim-dangmyeon, multteok and yubu-jumeoni (stuffed tofu pouches) all in one trip.
en.allergenNote: The fish cake and soy-sauce seasoning contain wheat and soy; the type of fish cake and toppings (kimchi, egg, etc.) vary by shop.

en.name: Jobang-nakji
en.summary: Busan-style spicy stir-fried octopus in a shallow broth, mixed into rice
en.ingredients: Nakji (long-arm octopus), onion, green onion, carrot, chili flakes and gochujang sauce, broth (nakgopsae adds beef gopchang and shrimp)
en.taste: A spicy-sweet sauce with just enough broth and bouncy octopus. Mixing it into rice mellows the heat.
en.origin: 'Jobang' is short for Joseon Bangjik (Joseon Textile), a mill in Busan's Beomil-dong during the Japanese colonial era; the area is still called 'Jobang' even though the factory is gone. The saucy octopus stir-fry that began at octopus restaurants in front of the mill came to be known as 'Jobang-nakji'.
steps: Put the pot or pan of octopus over the heat and wait until the sauce bubbles.
Put rice in a large bowl and top it with the seasoned bean sprouts and chives and the gim (seaweed) flakes served alongside.
Pour plenty of the octopus, sauce and all, over the rice and mix well.
If sauce is left over, add noodles (sari) or fried rice to finish.
en.tip: If you can't handle much spice, ask for it milder when ordering, and consider 'nakgopsae', which adds beef gopchang and shrimp to the octopus.
en.allergenNote: The gochujang and soy-sauce seasoning contain soy and wheat; ordering nakgopsae adds beef (gopchang) and shrimp, so check what the dish includes.

ja.ingredients: ナクチ(テナガダコ)、玉ねぎ、長ねぎ、にんじん、唐辛子粉・コチュジャンのたれ、だし(ナッコプセは牛ホルモン〈コプチャン〉とエビを追加)
ja.taste: 甘辛いたれのスープがほどよく残り、タコはぷりぷり。ご飯に混ぜると辛さがまろやかになる。
ja.origin: 「チョバン」は日本統治時代に釜山・凡一洞にあった朝鮮紡織の略称で、工場がなくなった今も凡一洞一帯は「チョバン」と呼ばれています。朝鮮紡織の前のナクチ店で始まった汁気のあるタコ炒めが、「チョバンナクチ」という名で定着しました。
steps: 鍋やフライパンに入ったタコ炒めを火にかけ、スープがぐつぐつ煮立つまで待つ。
大きな器にご飯を盛り、添えられた刻み海苔と豆もやし・ニラの和え物をのせる。
煮えたタコ炒めをスープごとたっぷりご飯にかけ、よく混ぜる。
たれが残ったら、麺(サリ)や焼き飯を追加して締める。
ja.tip: 辛いものが苦手なら注文時に辛さ控えめを頼みましょう。タコに牛ホルモンとエビを加えた「ナッコプセ」も検討してみてください。
ja.allergenNote: コチュジャン・醤油のたれに大豆・小麦が含まれます。ナッコプセを頼むと牛肉(ホルモン)とエビが加わるので、メニュー構成を確認してください。

en.name: Multteok
en.gloss: Rice cake skewers in fish-cake broth
en.summary: A Busan street snack: garaetteok skewers soaked soft in fish-cake broth
en.ingredients: Garaetteok (cylinder rice cakes), fish-cake broth (anchovy, kelp and radish stock), soy-sauce seasoning
en.taste: Having soaked up the fish-cake broth, it's soft outside and chewy inside, with a gently salty broth flavor.
en.origin: A Busan bunsik snack made by leaving rice cake skewers to soak for a long time in the fish-cake broth pot. No one is sure when it started, but it spread along with Busan fish cake, and it is counted as a Busan food that locals know well but people from other regions find unfamiliar.
steps: Take a multteok skewer that has softened after a long soak in the fish-cake pot.
Eat it as is, brush on a little soy-sauce seasoning, or dip it in tteokbokki sauce.
Pour some fish-cake broth into a paper cup and drink it alongside.
Don't throw away your skewers: keep them and pay by the number of sticks.
en.tip: The longer it has soaked, the softer it is, so pick a multteok from deep down in the pot.
en.allergenNote: The fish cakes simmered alongside and the soy-sauce seasoning bring in wheat and soy; depending on the fish cake, crustacean ingredients such as shrimp or crab may be mixed in.

zh.name: 水年糕
zh.summary: 在鱼饼汤里泡软的条状年糕串,釜山小吃
zh.ingredients: 条状年糕(garaetteok)、鱼饼汤(鳀鱼·海带·萝卜高汤)、酱油调味汁
zh.taste: 吸饱鱼饼汤后外软内韧,带着淡淡的咸鲜汤味。
zh.origin: 把年糕串放进鱼饼汤桶里长时间泡软来吃的釜山小吃。起源时间并不确定,但它随釜山鱼饼一同流行开来,被认为是釜山人很熟悉、其他地区的人却感到陌生的釜山食物。
steps: 从鱼饼汤桶里拿一串泡得软软的水年糕。
可以直接吃,也可以刷一点酱油调味汁,或蘸炒年糕酱汁吃。
用纸杯盛一杯鱼饼汤一起喝。
吃完的竹签不要扔,留着按数量结账。
zh.tip: 在汤里泡得越久越软,挑那些沉在汤桶深处的水年糕吧。
zh.allergenNote: 一起煮的鱼饼和酱油调味汁含小麦、大豆;依鱼饼种类不同,可能混有虾、蟹等甲壳类成分。

ja.name: ムルトック
ja.summary: オムク(おでん)のスープでじっくり柔らかくした棒餅の串。釜山の粉食
ja.ingredients: カレトック(棒状の餅)、オムクのスープ(煮干し・昆布・大根のだし)、醤油だれ
ja.taste: オムクのスープを吸って外はふんわり、中はもちもち。ほんのり塩気のあるスープの味が染みている。
ja.origin: オムクのスープの鍋に餅の串を入れて長く煮込んで食べる釜山の粉食です。いつ始まったかははっきりしませんが、釜山のオムクとともに広まり、釜山の人には身近でも他の地域では珍しい釜山の味として知られています。
steps: オムクの鍋で長く浸かって柔らかくなったムルトックの串を1本取る。
そのまま食べるか、醤油だれを少し塗る。トッポッキのソースにつけて食べることも。
紙コップにオムクのスープを注いで一緒に飲む。
食べ終えた串は捨てずに取っておき、本数で会計する。
ja.tip: スープに長く浸かっているほど柔らかいので、鍋の奥深くに沈んでいたムルトックを選びましょう。
ja.allergenNote: 一緒に煮るオムクと醤油だれに小麦・大豆が含まれます。オムクの種類によってはエビ・カニなどの甲殻類が含まれることがあります。

en.name: Yubu-jumeoni
en.summary: Kkangtong Market favorite: fried tofu pouches stuffed with japchae and tied with minari
en.ingredients: Fried tofu (yubu), glass noodles (dangmyeon), vegetables such as onion, carrot, spinach and mushrooms, seasoned meat, minari (water dropwort) as the tie, clear broth
en.taste: Mild and warming: chewy tofu pouches soaked in salty-savory broth, with a japchae filling
en.origin: First sold in the late 1990s at pojangmacha (street stalls) in Kkangtong Market, Bupyeong-dong, Jung-gu. Kkangtong Golmok Halmae Yubu Jeongol reportedly began as a street stall in 1998 and obtained a patent for its tofu pouch in 2002.
steps: Order yubu jeongol (tofu pouch hot pot) or eomuk-tang (fish cake soup) and the pouches arrive in hot broth.
Start with a spoonful of broth to taste its clean, refreshing flavor.
Split a pouch in half with chopsticks, take out the noodle filling, dip it lightly in soy sauce and eat it with the broth.
Add an order of bibim dangmyeon (spicy mixed glass noodles) for a full Kkangtong Market-style snack spread.
en.tip: The filling is very hot, so split the pouch in half and let the steam escape first.
en.allergenNote: The meat in the filling (pork or beef) varies by shop, and places that simmer the pouches with fish cakes may add crab or shrimp.

zh.name: 油豆腐福袋
zh.summary: 包着杂菜、用水芹扎口的油豆腐福袋，罐头市场名物
zh.ingredients: 油豆腐（yubu）、粉丝（dangmyeon）、洋葱·胡萝卜·菠菜·蘑菇等蔬菜、调味肉、水芹（扎口用）、清汤
zh.taste: 吸饱咸香汤汁的油豆腐软韧有嚼劲，与杂菜馅相融，清淡温暖
zh.origin: 这道小吃于20世纪90年代末开始在中区富平洞罐头市场（Kkangtong Market）的路边摊售卖。据悉，“罐头胡同奶奶油豆腐火锅”于1998年以路边摊起家，2002年凭油豆腐福袋取得专利。
steps: 点油豆腐火锅（yubu jeongol）或鱼糕汤，油豆腐福袋会泡在热汤里端上来。
先舀一勺汤，尝尝清爽的味道。
用筷子把福袋对半分开，取出粉丝馅，蘸少许酱油汁，配汤一起吃。
再点一份拌粉丝（bibim dangmyeon），享用罐头市场式小吃套餐。
zh.tip: 馅料非常烫，先对半分开散散热气再吃。
zh.allergenNote: 馅中所用肉类（猪肉或牛肉）因店而异；与鱼糕同煮的店可能含蟹、虾成分。

ja.summary: チャプチェを詰めた油揚げをセリで結んだ、カントン市場の名物
ja.ingredients: 油揚げ（ユブ）、春雨（タンミョン）、玉ねぎ・にんじん・ほうれん草・きのこなどの野菜、味付け肉、セリ（結びひも）、澄んだスープ
ja.taste: 塩気のあるスープを含んだもちっとした油揚げとチャプチェの具が合わさった、あっさり温かい味
ja.origin: 1990年代末、中区富平洞のカントン市場の屋台で売られ始めた料理です。「カントンコルモクハルメ ユブチョンゴル」は1998年に屋台として始まり、2002年にユブジュモニで特許を取得した店として知られています。
steps: ユブチョンゴル（油揚げ鍋）やおでんスープを頼むと、熱いスープに巾着が入って出てきます。
まずスープをひと口すくって、すっきりした味を確かめます。
巾着を箸で半分に割って春雨の具を取り出し、醤油だれに軽くつけてスープと一緒に食べます。
ピビムタンミョン（混ぜ春雨）も頼んで、カントン市場流の粉食セットを楽しみます。
ja.tip: 中身がとても熱いので、半分に割って一度湯気を逃がしてから食べてください。
ja.allergenNote: 具に入れる肉（豚肉・牛肉）は店によって異なり、おでんと一緒に煮る店ではカニ・エビ成分が加わることがあります。

en.name: Sogogi-gukbap
en.summary: Gyeongsang-style gukbap simmered spicy with radish and bean sprouts
en.ingredients: Beef (brisket, shank), radish, soybean sprouts, green onion, chili powder, guk-ganjang (soup soy sauce), minced garlic
en.taste: A clean, spicy chili broth with the sweetness of radish and the savory depth of long-simmered beef
en.origin: Gyeongsang-style beef soup, simmered spicy with radish, bean sprouts and chili powder, became established as a gukbap dish. In Busan, Haeundae Wonjo Halmae Gukbap, open since the early 1960s, is considered the classic old-timer.
steps: Taste the broth first; if it is too mild, add a little salt or dadaegi (chopped chili seasoning) bit by bit.
Mix the rice into the soup, or for ttaro-gukbap (rice served separately), add it a spoonful at a time.
Scoop up beef, bean sprouts and radish together in one spoonful.
Finish with kkakdugi (cubed radish kimchi) or musaengchae (spicy shredded radish) for a refreshing end.
en.tip: Many diners come for a hangover cure, so go a little early, before the lunch rush, to wait less.
en.allergenNote: Shops using brewed soy sauce or dadaegi (chili paste) may include wheat, and some also add seonji (coagulated ox blood).

zh.name: 牛肉汤饭
zh.summary: 加萝卜、豆芽熬煮的庆尚道式辣牛肉汤饭
zh.ingredients: 牛肉（牛胸肉·牛腱）、萝卜、黄豆芽、大葱、辣椒粉、汤用酱油（guk-ganjang）、蒜末
zh.taste: 辣椒粉带出的辛辣爽口汤头，融合萝卜的清甜与炖烂牛肉的鲜香
zh.origin: 将牛肉与萝卜、豆芽、辣椒粉一起煮得香辣的庆尚道式牛肉汤，逐渐发展成了汤饭。在釜山，自1960年代初营业至今的“海云台元祖奶奶汤饭”被视为代表性老店。
steps: 先尝汤，觉得淡可少量逐次加盐或辣味调料（dadaegi）。
把米饭泡进汤里吃；若是饭汤分开上的“ttaro-gukbap”，就一勺一勺把饭放进汤里。
把牛肉、豆芽和萝卜舀在同一勺里一起吃。
配萝卜块泡菜（kkakdugi）或凉拌萝卜丝，清爽收尾。
zh.tip: 来醒酒的客人很多，避开午餐时间稍早前往，等位较短。
zh.allergenNote: 使用酿造酱油或辣酱料（dadaegi）的店可能含小麦，也有店会加入牛血块（seonji）。

en.name: Gijang Myeolchi-ssambap
en.summary: Gijang's spring anchovies braised spicy and eaten wrapped in greens
en.ingredients: Fresh large anchovies from Daebyeon Port in Gijang, ugeoji and siraegi (dried greens), chili powder, doenjang (soybean paste), garlic, green chili, lettuce, napa cabbage and perilla leaves for wrapping
en.taste: Tender, rich fresh anchovy in a spicy, salty sauce, balanced by crisp wrap greens
en.origin: Daebyeon Port in Gijang is one of Korea's leading anchovy grounds, famous for large anchovies caught with drift gillnets in spring. A fishing-village dish of freshly caught anchovies braised spicy with ugeoji and eaten as wraps became the signature of the port's raw-fish restaurant street, and the Gijang Anchovy Festival is held every spring.
steps: Place a spoonful of rice on a lettuce or cabbage leaf.
Pick one or two anchovies and some ugeoji from the braise and lay them on the rice.
Add green chili and garlic, wrap it up and eat it in one bite.
Finish by mixing rice into the leftover sauce; it is even better with an order of myeolchi-hoe (raw anchovy).
en.tip: Go in April–May, peak spring anchovy season, when the fish are plumpest, to taste it at its best.
en.allergenNote: Anchovy is not a labeled allergen, but gochujang and fish sauce blends vary by shop and may contain wheat or shrimp.

zh.name: 机张鳀鱼包饭
zh.summary: 将机张春季鳀鱼炖得香辣、用菜叶包着吃的特色美味
zh.ingredients: 机张大边港新鲜大鳀鱼、干菜叶（ugeoji·siraegi）、辣椒粉、大酱、大蒜、青辣椒、包饭用生菜·白菜·苏子叶
zh.taste: 辛辣咸香的酱汁裹着软嫩鲜香的鳀鱼肉，配上爽脆的包饭菜叶
zh.origin: 机张大边港是韩国代表性的鳀鱼产地，以春季用流刺网捕捞的大个鳀鱼闻名。渔村人把刚捕上来的鲜鳀鱼与干菜叶一起炖得香辣、包菜叶吃，这道渔家菜成了大边港生鱼片街的招牌，每年春天还会举办机张鳀鱼节。
steps: 在生菜或白菜叶上放一勺米饭。
从炖锅里夹一两条鳀鱼和干菜叶，放在饭上。
配上青辣椒和大蒜包好，一口吃下。
最后用剩下的酱汁拌饭收尾；加点一份鳀鱼生鱼片（myeolchi-hoe）更好。
zh.tip: 鱼肉最肥美的4~5月春季鳀鱼季前往，才能尝到真正的味道。

ja.name: 機張ミョルチサムパプ
ja.gloss: カタクチイワシ煮の葉包みご飯
ja.summary: 機張の春カタクチイワシをピリ辛に煮て、葉野菜で包んで食べる名物
ja.ingredients: 機張・大辺港の生カタクチイワシ（大羽）、ウゴジ・シレギ（干し菜）、粉唐辛子、テンジャン（味噌）、にんにく、青唐辛子、包み用のサンチュ・白菜・エゴマの葉
ja.taste: ピリ辛で塩気のあるたれに、柔らかく香ばしい生イワシの身とシャキシャキの包み野菜が合わさった味
ja.origin: 機張の大辺港は、春に刺し網で獲る大ぶりのカタクチイワシで知られる韓国屈指の産地です。獲れたての生イワシを干し菜と一緒にピリ辛に煮て葉で包んで食べていた漁村料理が、大辺港の刺身店街の名物となり、毎年春には機張ミョルチ（イワシ）祭りが開かれます。
steps: サンチュや白菜の葉にご飯をひと匙のせます。
イワシ煮からイワシ1～2尾とウゴジを取り、ご飯の上にのせます。
青唐辛子とにんにくを添えて包み、ひと口で食べます。
残った煮汁にご飯を混ぜて締め、ミョルチフェ（イワシの刺身）も頼むとさらに楽しめます。
ja.tip: 身がいちばん太る4～5月の春イワシの時期に行ってこそ、本来の味が楽しめます。
ja.allergenNote: カタクチイワシは表示対象ではありませんが、店ごとにコチュジャンや魚醤の配合が異なり、小麦やエビ成分が含まれることがあります。

en.name: Yeongdo Haenyeo-chon Jeonbok-juk
en.summary: Green-tinged porridge made with abalone gathered by haenyeo divers, innards and all
en.ingredients: Abalone (meat and innards), soaked rice, sesame oil, salt
en.taste: Mild and comforting: a deep ocean aroma from the abalone innards, nutty sesame oil and soft, swollen rice
en.origin: Most of Yeongdo's haenyeo (women divers) are chulhyang haenyeo who came over from Jeju, or their descendants; Jeju divers are said to have first arrived in Yeongdo around 1887. At the Haenyeo Village on the first floor of the Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall, by the sea at Jungni in Dongsam-dong, the divers clean and serve the abalone, sea squirt, sea cucumber and other catches from that day's dive.
steps: At the haenyeo village, start with an assorted platter of sea squirt, sea cucumber, abalone and more.
The porridge is hot, so eat it a little at a time from the edge of the bowl.
Add gim (seaweed) flakes or sesame oil to taste, or enjoy it with kimchi.
Alternate with seafood ramyeon or sea urchin gimbap while taking in the sea view.
en.tip: Hours and menu can change with the weather and diving conditions, so call ahead on windy days.
en.allergenNote: Shops that season with soup soy sauce or top it with egg or gim flakes may add soy or egg.

zh.name: 影岛海女村鲍鱼粥
zh.summary: 用海女采来的鲍鱼连内脏一起熬成的翠绿色粥
zh.ingredients: 鲍鱼（肉与内脏）、泡发的大米、香油、盐
zh.taste: 鲍鱼内脏带出浓郁海味，配上香油的醇香与软糯米粒，口味温和
zh.origin: 影岛海女大多是从济州岛离乡迁来的海女（出乡海女）及其后代，据传约1887年济州海女来到影岛是其开端。在东三洞中里海边的影岛海女文化展示馆1楼海女村，海女们会把当天潜水采到的鲍鱼、海鞘、海参等现场处理后端上桌。
steps: 在海女村先点一份海鞘、海参、鲍鱼等海鲜拼盘。
鲍鱼粥很烫，从碗边一点点舀着吃。
可按口味加海苔碎或香油，或配泡菜吃。
与海鲜拉面或海胆紫菜包饭交替着吃，欣赏海景。
zh.tip: 营业和菜单可能随天气与潜水情况变化，风大的日子请先打电话确认。
zh.allergenNote: 用汤用酱油调味或撒鸡蛋、海苔碎的店，可能含大豆或蛋类。

ja.name: 影島海女村のアワビ粥
ja.gloss: 肝ごと炊いたアワビ粥
ja.summary: 海女が獲ったアワビを肝ごと炊いた緑色のお粥
ja.ingredients: アワビ（身と肝）、浸水させた米、ごま油、塩
ja.taste: アワビの肝から出る濃い磯の香りに香ばしいごま油、柔らかくふくらんだ米粒が合わさったやさしい味
ja.origin: 影島の海女の多くは済州島から渡ってきた海女（出郷海女）とその子孫で、1887年ごろ済州の海女が影島に来たのが始まりと伝えられています。東三洞・中里の海辺にある影島海女文化展示館1階の海女村では、海女たちがその日に潜って獲ったアワビ・ホヤ・ナマコなどをその場でさばいて出してくれます。
steps: 海女村でホヤ・ナマコ・アワビなどの海鮮盛り合わせをまず頼みます。
アワビ粥は熱いので、器のふちから少しずつすくって食べます。
好みで刻みのりやごま油を足したり、キムチを添えたりします。
海鮮ラーメンやウニのキンパと交互に食べながら海の景色を楽しみます。
ja.tip: 天候や潜水の状況で営業やメニューが変わることがあるので、風の強い日は事前に電話で確認してください。
allergens: 貝類（カキ・アワビ・ムール貝を含む）
